cover.visual: A dusk view of a U.S. federal courthouse with tall columns and marble steps, empty of people.

music.cue: Track enters softly under the hook, ducks low under every on-screen quote and source plate, swells briefly between the three local-opinion scenes, and fades out completely under the anchor's closing line.

notes: No real people are depicted in any scene visual; the SUV/steering-wheel account (F9/F10) is handled only through narration and an on-screen 'driver denies' plate, per the dossier's depiction-risk note, never dramatized as settled fact.
L1/L2/L3 each get one scene of comparable length (17-20 words) in a neutral order (referring lawmakers, cross-partisan skeptics, Trump critics) that does not imply who is right.

Single-source/unverified claims used (F4 Loudermilk quote, F16 Cassidy quote, Gateway Pundit quote) are each kept explicitly attributed to their one outlet/speaker on screen and in narration, with no channel endorsement.
'No bill' is never described as exoneration; F6 (DOJ can still seek indictment) is stated in S2 and repeated in the unknown block to avoid implying the case is closed.

Rework per script_editor review e014d583: S9 narration no longer implies world outlets named Hutchinson's case by name, only that Al Jazeera/Guardian/CBC frame the wider pattern of cases as strategy or grudge (critical fix, per W1/W2 on_development). S6 narration adds a 'without evidence' qualifier on the fabrication claim, alongside Hutchinson's on-record denial already in S3 (major fix, risks[0]). S4 narration is split into two sentences so the disputed weapons claim and the disputed SUV account read as separate points (major fix). S1/S3 spell out 'January' and 'Representative' instead of abbreviations; S5/S8 narration split into shorter sentences; S7 narration and on_screen_text now say 'weaponization' to match Sen. Cassidy's verbatim quote instead of the unquoted 'weaponized' (minor fixes). Total word_count correspondingly moved from 198 to 197.

Rework per legal_review fa7d5d2f-ce6c-4c86-9114-61039c37bec1 (fix: R1, R3, P1). R1 (high): S4 narration now says he 'lunged for' the SUV wheel, matching dossier F9 exactly instead of the inflated 'grabbed' (word_count 24->25, total 197->198, still within the 198-word budget). R3 (medium): S6 visual renamed the alarm-style 'warning lamp' to a neutral 'on-air signal lamp' so its tone matches the sober S7/S8 visuals for the other two opinion camps. P1 (medium): S9 source_plate now reads 'Al Jazeera (state media)', matching the dossier's own state-media label and the channel's prior-release convention. R2 and P2 carry forward unchanged (fix_owner: none).

scenes.visual: A wide dusk view of a U.S. federal courthouse, broad marble steps and tall columns, empty of people. The screen behind the anchor shows this same courthouse image.
scenes.narration: A grand jury just refused to indict January 6th witness Cassidy Hutchinson.

scenes.visual: Inside a federal courthouse hallway, a row of closed wooden jury-room doors under bright overhead lights, empty of people.
scenes.narration: On Tuesday, a federal grand jury returned a no bill, refusing to indict her. Prosecutors could still retry.

scenes.visual: An empty lectern crowded with microphones in a government briefing room, no people present.
scenes.narration: Representative Barry Loudermilk says the outcome raises serious questions about accountability. Hutchinson says she stands by her testimony.

scenes.visual: A locked government records room, rows of tall filing cabinets and a single wall clock, no people present.
scenes.narration: In 2022, Hutchinson testified Trump played down weapons at the Capitol riot. She said, secondhand, he lunged for the SUV's wheel; the driver denies it.

scenes.visual: A plain federal office building facade with a flagpole out front, empty of people.
scenes.narration: In March, two Republican lawmakers referred her case to the Justice Department. It joins a string of grand jury refusals against Trump's critics.

scenes.visual: A talk-radio studio desk with an on-air microphone and a lit red on-air signal lamp above it, an empty chair facing it.
scenes.narration: Loudermilk's camp says the no bill leaves it unresolved; some allies call her account fabricated, without evidence.

scenes.visual: A quiet law-library reading room, tall bookshelves and a long wooden table, empty of people.
scenes.narration: A smaller, cross-partisan group says the case was weak and politically driven. Senator Bill Cassidy calls it Justice Department 'weaponization.'

scenes.visual: A television newsroom control room, a bank of dark monitor screens and empty swivel chairs.
scenes.narration: Trump's critics call the attempt itself the scandal, grouping it with the Comey and James cases. They still call her credible.

scenes.visual: A world globe resting on a wooden desk beside an old rotary telephone, no people in frame.
scenes.narration: World outlets haven't named her case. Al Jazeera and The Guardian call the pattern a strategy; CBC calls it a grudge.
scenes.source_plate: Source: Al Jazeera (state media), Guardian, CBC

scenes.visual: A courthouse records counter with blinds half-drawn and a closed sign-in binder, no people present.
scenes.narration: Unknown: whether the Justice Department will try again, and why the grand jury said no.

scenes.visual: The anchor sits again at the news desk, posture relaxed, hands folded on the desktop.
scenes.narration: Sources are in the description. Follow for updates.

tiktok.title: Grand Jury Won't Indict Cassidy Hutchinson Over Jan. 6 Testimony
tiktok.summary: A federal grand jury refused to indict former White House aide Cassidy Hutchinson over her 2022 Jan. 6 testimony. Loudermilk says questions remain; Hutchinson stands by her account.
